title: Metal: push constants re-applied by compute_list_add_barrier() overwrite the next pipeline's uniform set (GPU page fault, timeout waiting for fence freeze)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.8.dev7.official [c971f93e7]
- Not tested, but the same code path exists in 4.6.3-stable, 4.7.2-stable and current master (e7cfa294a0). See "Cause" below.

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev7 - macOS Unknown (27.0.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor (3024x1964 @ 120.00 Hz) - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M4 Pro (14 threads) - 24.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

On Metal, if `compute_list_add_barrier()` is followed by a dispatch of a pipeline that has **no** push constants, that pipeline's uniform set gets overwritten. The overwrite happens at the Metal buffer index where the *previous* pipeline kept its push constants. The other drivers are not affected, because push constants there do not share slots with descriptor sets.

In the MRP this only produces a wrong result. In a real project the overwritten set held 20 sampled textures (a 320-byte argument buffer). The shader then read texture handles out of the 16 bytes of push constant data, which caused `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorPageFault`. After that, Metal ignores every further command buffer (`kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorSubmissionsIgnored`), and the engine freezes with an endless stream of:

```
ERROR: timeout waiting for fence
   at: wait (drivers/metal/rendering_device_driver_metal3.cpp:58)
```

The freeze happened at random, but the overwrite happened on every frame.

#### Cause

1. `RenderingDevice::compute_list_add_barrier()` ends the compute list, begins a new one, and re-records the previous pipeline, uniform sets **and push constants** ([rendering_device.cpp#L7197-L7216](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp#L7197-L7216)).
2. During replay, `MDCommandBufferBase::encode_push_constant_data()` stores the data, sets `push_constant_binding` to the push constant index of the *previous* shader (index 1 here, because that shader only has set 0), and sets `DIRTY_PUSH` ([metal_objects_shared.cpp#L703-L728](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/drivers/metal/metal_objects_shared.cpp#L703-L728)).
3. The caller binds a different pipeline. `MDCommandBuffer::bind_pipeline()` marks the pipeline and the uniform sets dirty, but leaves `DIRTY_PUSH` and `push_constant_binding` untouched ([metal3_objects.cpp#L431-L437](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/drivers/metal/metal3_objects.cpp#L431-L437)).
4. On dispatch, `_compute_set_dirty_state()` first binds the new uniform sets (set 1 goes to buffer index 1). It then still sees `DIRTY_PUSH` and calls `setBytes(push_constant_data, 16, push_constant_binding = 1)`, which overwrites set 1 ([metal3_objects.cpp#L1616-L1639](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/drivers/metal/metal3_objects.cpp#L1616-L1639)).

If the next pipeline has push constants of its own, they replace the stale ones before the dispatch. That is why only push-constant-less pipelines are affected.

#### Possible fix

When `bind_pipeline()` switches to a pipeline with a different shader, drop any pending push constants: clear `DIRTY_PUSH` and reset `push_constant_binding`. This matches the RD contract, because `RenderingDevice` already requires push constants to be supplied again after a shader change (`pipeline_push_constant_supplied = false`, [rendering_device.cpp#L6852-L6856](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c971f93e7e76b0ef919bf6009e7b868bea04db7f/servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp#L6852-L6856)). The render branch of `bind_pipeline()` and `_render_set_dirty_state()` have the same structure.

#### Workaround

Before a dispatch without push constants, end the compute list and begin a new one instead of calling `compute_list_add_barrier()`.

Possibly related: #119436 (same freeze symptom, but the trigger there appears to be long-running compute work).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached MRP on a Mac with the Metal driver.
2. Run the main scene. Expected output: `OK` twice. Actual output:
   ```
   Separate compute lists: OK (1234)
   compute_list_add_barrier: WRONG (0, expected 1234)
   ```
3. Optional: run with `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 MTL_DEBUG_LAYER_ERROR_MODE=nslog`. Metal then reports that buffer slot 1 holds the 16-byte push constant block instead of set 1:
   ```
   Compute Function(main0): argument spvDescriptorSet1[0] from Buffer(1) with offset(0) and length(16) has space for 16 bytes, but argument has a length(24).
   ```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The MRP dispatches a producer (set 0 + 16-byte push constant) and then a consumer (set 0 + set 1, no push constants) in one compute list. Between them it either calls `compute_list_add_barrier()` or ends the list and begins a new one.

[metal-push-constant-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33003051/metal-push-constant-mrp.zip)
